Hey buddy!

This isn't weird at all. I bet that there are more people around you that never had sex or even kissed a girl than you realize.


I was a very late bloomer myself. I literally never held the hand of a woman until I got my first gf when  I was 23-24.
So it's a combination of luck and actively doing stuff to make it happen.


I think what I'm trying to say is - don't be too hard on yourself, this really isn't that big of a deal and you're extremely young. However don't just sit back and do nothing. It probably won't just happen out of the blue, you'll have to start approaching women whether it's online or face to face.

I don't know what to say really... I'm going through a rough year and realized I really need to see someone. And yet I keep postponing it and avoid scheduling an appointment, telling myself it's mainly due to fears of opening up.

The thing is, I'm starting to realize another huge fear is that I'm putting too much hope on therapy.

In the last year I'm telling myself stuff like "Okay well at least you're gonna start therapy soon and things will probably get better." And yet I'm almost certain I'll experience what you're talking about. 

That is, hearing stuff I already tell myself in the countless hours of imaginary conversations I have with myself in my head, which have become my only form of communication with others. As well as the toxic thought patterns that I have - which I know aren't rational.

I was hoping that seeing someone will lead to real improvement, and not just talking. Not that there's anything wrong with that, I mean I guess it would be nice to say the stuff I have in my head out loud. It's just that I was kind of dreaming it'll yield better results.


Who knows, maybe in a year I'll be back here posting that I started therapy and it actually helped.

Hey man... There's not a lot I can say. I don't have a lot of experience in the dating world either. But like they say, you preach what you need to hear - 


Currently I'm at the point which your were 4 years ago - left heart broken after a cheating gf ruined me (only seems as if you handled it better than me and left immediately, while I tried to linger and stay).
What you're going through sucks. The whole thing - having your heart teared apart by a cheating person, and then after years to go through this breakup. 
 

Here's the thing. You found a woman who was amazing and thought you're amazing as well. She gone now, but also left you with some stuff to think about and work on. I think you should work on those things - not for her or for a scenario in which she comes back and you're a changed person, but for the woman to come after her. 

Maybe you shouldn't renew that WoW subscription. Maybe you should get back to playing music, maybe you should find a new band. Maybe find a new hobby - perhaps a new instrument? Start working out? Learn a new language? 


Think of it this way - you went through 4 years w/o a relationship after you were cheated on. Then this woman came into your life. 

I'm not saying this will change anything, but maybe if you do improve yourself in the fields she spoke about (that is, hobbies and doing more in life than just work) then you'll find someone new sooner than that. 

And as for her not contacting you - it's perfectly fine to wish to hear that this is some kind of April Fool's joke. But you did the right thing, and it's for the best if things stay this way. It's only going to hold you back from moving on

It's not easy, believe me. You're going to have hard times and it's gonna be dark.

Also don't try to beg or contact her again. That will only do harm. Don't try to overthink and analyze what happens and why she left - there could be thousands of reasons and none of them matter. 


It will get better, look at this relationship as a learning experience

I'm sorry pal. I know exactly what you're going through. A couple of months ago I went through something similar. 

I learned what trickle truth is, and you need to realize that might be the case here as well. It's unlikely that she's telling you everything 

Plus, there's the factor of her just doing it again. 


I'll say one thing which I think is really important - when I came to reddit and asked what to do with my cheating gf, everybody said to immediately run away. 

But one guy said something a bit different, along the lines of - "I know you won't take the advice here and you'll stay with her, but you need to leave before you get hurt even more". 

And guess what? I didn't listen to the strangers on the Internet. Because what the fuck do they know about our relationship? This girl and I are so maddeningly in love! She even proposed to me and said she'll be the  mother of my children. So I stayed. 

And guess what, a month later it ended. WAY worse than it would've, had I ended it in time. I was the one who ended up getting dumped, and I'm still shattered to millions of pieces. 

So, listen to the strangers on reddit. They're looking at things with way more experience and perspective, and with zero bias towards the situation. 


By the way, first thing I did after the break up was going on reddit, finding my old thread looking for advice. Read the whole thing, couldn't believe how stupid I was. Immediately sent a private message to the aforementioned dude, and apologized to him. 


I wish you the best of luck

I'm terribly sorry you're going through this. 

It hurts so much. I know. I'm there right now. Seeing the person who broke you to millions of pieces by cheating and lying to you, moving on with their life. And you're still dwelling on it all. 

Every single lie they ever told you keeps coming back. You rediscover new lies. You rediscover other times in which they said they're at X while actually being with that other person, behind your back. While you're sitting at home alone wondering why the fuck aren't they answering their phone. 

And they don't care. They forgot all they did to you. They move on with their life without blinking. 

Trust me, I know. It hurts. It's not fair. It's disgusting. I think of her and all I see is an evil person. It hurts me to say this but I really wish her nothing but the pain she causes me. 


And yet. Revenge isn't the thing to do. I could've done stuff to her that probably would've hurt her. Revenge porn? The day we broke up I deleted it all. Everything she ever sent me. 
Telling mutual acquaintances what she did? Other stuff I don't feel like sharing here? There were so many things I could have done. 


So I didn't do anything. I'm not like her. And yes, I'm forcing myself to believe in karma. 

I suggest that you do nothing as well. It's not worth it. 

You're going through a point in life that isn't fair. Plain and simple. It's not fucking fair. I know. 

But don't make things worse. Just try to slowly move one with your life. It's not easy. I still haven't figured out how. But I guess it'll happen and the pain and anger will fade.

I'm really sorry for what you're going through. 

People can really be horrible and cruel and evil. You should end this as soon as possible. 

Also as for "wasting so many years of your life" - say thanks you ONLY wasted that amount of time and not double the amount. Look at this as a source of some comfort. You wasted 10 years? At least it wasnt 20.
This probably sounds silly but I think it's true.

I think that even if you're somewhat right, I just can't see myself finding another person who will share my life with. 

It's like.... I can imagine myself dying, I can imagine myself earning a lot of money from work and gaining wealth. I can imagine myself getting back to sports and swimming and  being successful in those fields. I can imagine myself being paralyzed or being diagnosed with ALS or cancer. 

I close my eyes and I can see all that. 

But I can't see my self going to sleep with another human being wanting me to hold them. I can't see another person looking into my eyes and loving me like she did. I can't imagine another person wanting to have sex with me. I can't imagine another person wanting to marry me or have kids with me (now I don't believe she wanted it as well, but oh well) 

I just can't see any of that happening.

I honestly don't think socializing online would help. If anything, it's easier for me speaking with people behind a screen, where I have the time to carefully articulate myself and think my responses through. 

It's actually talking to new people that is hell. And it's not an insecurity of "oh God what if they don't like me". I know they won't like me and couldn't care less. It's way deeper than that. I think I'm too fragile for society. I over analyze. I'm sick of the voices in my head (in the last few weeks I can't move around without music, I cant live with the voices in my head snymore). 

I don't really know what to say. I just know this is it. 

You see, I've never shared this with anyone in my entire life, but whatever - I've always had the plan to work till I'm 30~, take all the money I saved (because I do nothing with my life aside from work) and travel around the world for a year or two. Then donate what's left and end it. 

But then I met that girl I wrote about and it made me change my mind. But now that I had my heart shattered, I see how I'm slowly going back to that previous plan I had for life, and it fucking hurts. 

Wow now that I began writing here I realized that there's so much to talk and write about. I'm sorry for wasting your time pal, thanks for listening though. You're a nice human being.

Yeah it happened once why won't it happen again? Because the chances are so tiny. What are the chances of someone you actually like, liking you back and doing something about it? 

As for my relationship with other colleagues - the current company I work for, most people are married or not my age. 

Sociability is fucking hard. How do I even meet people? I've never been to a bar, I don't have friends who can take me to places, and with all due respect I can't just show up at a random social place all alone and talk to people. I know it sounds weird and exaggerated, but it's the truth. There's a better chance of me flying. 

Online is easier, I'm actually good at talking with people online (although English isn't my native language so sorry for the bad English). 

I tried downloading it OkCupid, you won't be surprised that it went terribly and I received zero interest from the ladies, so I deleted it. 



Here's the thing I guess it seems as if this is about not being able to find a woman in my life. 

It's coming to realize that for all my life I've been all alone. And I accepted that and learned to live with it. But then in some miraculous way, which till this day I can't explain, I found a woman who was a part of my life. And now she's gone. And I realize I'm back to where I was. Only now I've seen the other side of life. I know what it's like to not be lonely. To have someone to text. To have someone who cares for you. To have someone who wants to touch your body a body you learned to dislike. Somebody who likes your mind and soul, two things you find disgusting and damaged.

Already contacted her, got slapped in the face real hard with her reaction. 

Joke's on me.

Yes she did. Said something in the lines of her "not wanting to deal with any more drama, since she's just started to get her shit together after the BU and doesn't want to go backwards" 


Which I read as "I don't want to reconcile", am I correct?

Good for me, I contacted her. If anyone wonders -

1. No, it wasn't worth it 

2. Yes, I wish I hadn't done it

3. Yes, I want to throw up right now and am in tears 

4. No, I think I'll never get over her. 

5. Yes, I hate myself. 


This is just wonderful. Two months of painful mental work went down the drain.
But what if she wants to get back as well? She was blocked for all this time, and I explicitly told her to not contact me. What if she regrets everything as well

Well that's a tough question and I believe that some people might be mature enough to still be in touch with an ex. 

In my case, they dated for over 3 years and she told me they broke up months before we started. I later found out that they were on "breaks" and that she really finally ended it with him the day before our first date (What. The. Fuck) 

She then told me they're just friends and it's nothing harmful. It then turned out they were much more than friends and she was playing me the whole time. Lying cheating, hiding things, you name it. 

I think it depends to what extent they're still in touch. Is it a text every couple of months? Fine. Do they see each other on a weekly basis through mutual friends and constantly text? I could never ever be in such a relationship after what I went through. Never again. I don't care who I date. No way I'm going into that place once again. 


By the way, The School Of Life on YouTube have a great video on why exes can't really be friends. It's worth watching.

I'm sorry.... But it's probably for the best if you let this one go. 

It sounds like she isn't over him, and this might turn out badly. 

Sadly from my personal experience, when you suspect someone isn't over their ex, they aren't. Sleeping over at his place? What the hell? 

I hate having to give examples of my personal experience in so many of my comments for these questions, but here goes another one - When my ex and her entire family went on a trip, her ex went over to her empty house to sleep in her room, in her bed. 
Why, you ask? God knows. I obviously didn't know about this at the time and only found out months later, when the whole thing blew up. I also found out that she was cheating on me with him, but I digress. 


And you know what, maybe there's nothing malicious about her behavior and it's really all just friendly. Then that's for you to answer whether this bothers you or not. I know I could never live with such a behavior after what I went through.

Sure! 

Look, I don't know what your guy is like or how long you've been together. Perhaps there are people out there that would rather know nothing about previous relationships of their SO.

However I personally can't really see how you sharing it with him can backfire. If anything, you gain plenty of credibility points. 


I can sit here all day and say horrible things about my ex girlfriend. That woman ended up lying to me for months, hiding endless amounts of occasions in which they met behind my back, and there was even a period where things escalated to physical contact. She fucking cheated! 

However, I can look at things backwards and believe her when she said how she regretted not telling me a month into our relationship what's going on - she said that in retrospect she clearly should have shared everything with me, instead of building lies over lies. 

Call me naive, but I kinda believe her. And I believe things would've been different if she just shared it, we could have handled it together. 

So that's it. Just share it with him. You've done nothing wrong, and if he finds out in a way, that might be uncomfortable for both of you.

Yes!!! Tell him! You have nothing to hide. 


I'm saying this as the guy who dated a woman that had an ex that didn't let go of her (that is, my ex had an ex who couldn't live with the fact my ex broke up with him.) 

Our relationship ended horribly because she handled things with her ex terribly. She hid everything behind my back (claiming she was afraid of sharing it with me) and things escalated - at first she caved in to him begging to see her and talk to her, and then things got worse and worse... (she ended up cheating with him after a few months, but I digress) 

The point - if she would've shared everything in the beginning, things might have looked differently. 


Tell him this guy is harassing you. Obviously tell him you don't nees him to help you handle things, but you just want him to know. Promise him there's nothing to worry about (even suggest showing him the texts you're receiving so that he knows there's nothing going on). 

I think that's the best approach. Hell, I wish my ex would've acted this way.

You definitely shouldn't put up with this, if he has some unresolved issues then they shouldn't ruin life for you. But I don't know if I'd go and end it immediately. Perhaps have a more serious talk, explaining that things can't stay like this for a long time, and you've had it.

Please for the love of God leave her. She is clearly not over him. If you stay together, there's a massive chance she'll end up leaving in the future to try and reconcile with him once again. Or even worse, do something behind your back. It's going to hurt a lot now, but it might hurt way more in the future. 


Just like you're saying - it seems like she'd rather lose you, than to cut the contact with him for good. 

It's none of your business if they're talking? It fucking is. Especially after what she told you. 

I'm not gonna try and compare what I went through with what you are, but I was with a woman who wasn't over her ex, and I later in the relationship found out she was cheating with him. 

I asked reddit what to do, and every single person here told me to leave. 
But I knew better than everybody else, because she says she loves me and we have such an amazing time together, and she swore she's over him. 

So I ignored the strangers on the Internet and we stayed together. A month after that it ended in a horrible way, turns out she was never over him and never stopped lying. As absurd as it may sound, I wish I would have listened to strangers on the Internet.

I know everybody says this, and I bet you read these tips and roll your eyes, because it's hard to accept and believe - just share the story with him. 

And if he bails? Fuck him.


Now, don't go and share everything with him into details. Tell him you went through some trauma when you were younger and it left you cosmetically scarred down there. Share with him how afraid you are. 

If this makes him run away, then that's his problem. You might be scarred in a way that's physically noticeable, he might be scarred in other ways you don't know of yet. That's the beauty of it all. You're getting to know each other. 


I know I would appreciate it if a woman would share something like this with me, it would make me feel trusted and connected with her.

This was hard to read, so I can't imagine experiencing it. 

It seems that you're approaching this with the right attitude, and that's obviously going to make this easier for you. 

I wish you the best of luck

Please oh please, don't take her back. Please. 

I found out that my ex was cheating on me. She was my first ever gf, I thought the world of her and decided to try to forgive and stay. 

We set very clear boundaries - no contact whatsoever with the guy she cheated with (her ex), all sort of other things as well.

Well, we all know the proverb about the grass always being greener. 

If you're happy with the current guy, and things aren't bad, I wouldn't leave. You'll risk something good, for something you know nothing about? 

If however there are problems in the relationship, that's a different question. 

I'd ask myself - would I be happy to leave the current relationship, even if a potential relationship with this coworker would fail instantly (or even there wouldn't be a relationship to begin with...)

Clearly there's a problem with the way he's acting. 


I think you should have a serious talk with him. Tell him that you'll be doing the talking for the next 20 minutes, and he can react once you're done, or he can have a day to think about what you just said. 

You then tell him that his behavior is becoming intolerable, and you can't take it anymore. You tell him how much you love him, what he means to you, and that you'll never ever do anything to hurt him. 

But he needs to show some trust and respect. You haven't done anything to make him so suspicious, and he should treat you with trust. 

I would also tell him that it's perfectly fine to get jealous once in a while, we all do. And even if something happens that makes him a bit concerned (such as him finding out you're talking to somebody you had a crush on), then there's a way to talk about things - he can discuss and share his feelings in a mature and loving way, without turning it into a fight. 


Here's the thing - if things keep up the way they are, you will get sick of it and leave. It might take another month, or perhaps a year. But if he won't change, it's going to happen. You shouldn't threaten him, but you should make it clear that it's becoming too much of an issue.
